summary: Penghao Sun specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He completed his doctoral studies under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, having also studied under scholars including Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Jay Jasanoff, and Qingying Chen (2009–2011).
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang as well as Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, whom he also taught.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Palyul Monastery, under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1960–1991), and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt (~1936–1950) and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Copenhagen (1971–~1990) under Erik Haarh, he held posts at Copenhagen (1982–1989), Leipzig University (1994–2017), and UC Berkeley (2017).

Per Kværne (b. 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. After earning his degrees at the University of Oslo (~1965–1973), he taught at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as professor at Oslo (1975–2007).

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1977–1998) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2012).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Rau from around 1968 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Marburg from circa 1971 to 1991.

Perry Link (b. 1944) is a sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and UC Riverside (~2008) as Chancellorial Chair Professor.

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) studied at the University of Munich (~1974–1996), where he also held a post (~1988–1998). He served as professor at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson (b. 1972) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2000), and later held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter Bisschop specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, later serving as Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Editor at Leiden University.

Peter Connolly works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (b. 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. A Yale University graduate, he studied under Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, and directed the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center.
Peter Dronke (1934–2020) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Magdalen College (~1955–1961) and held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1961 to 2001.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford, where he conducted his research under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Advised by Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, he also studied under Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki (b. 1950) studied at Oxford (MSc, DPhil 1975–1979). Specializing in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and the University of Cambridge (~1985–2017).

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Mainz in 1952, studying under Ernst Schwarz. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
